cluster_thesis.text: Downgraded from strengthening (09-09) to intact. Demand evidence is unchanged -- all three members raised FY26 guidance this summer (GEV 09-14, BE third raise to $3.9-4.2B, VRT raised EPS mid to ~$6.70) -- but two new facts show backlog is not near-term margin: GLJ's vintage math says GEV's 2027 deliveries carry ~3pp backlog margin vs 10-11pp on the 2028 vintage, and VRT missed Q2 revenue by ~$110M on supply-chain/execution timing, not orders. Monday's -7.5% cluster move was mostly factor (AI-slowdown essay + 10Y +32bps/1m), not demand: VRT -7.7% and BE -6.8% fell almost as much as GEV -8.6% with no vintage exposure. Mid innings: turbine price resets monetize in 2028, not 2027.
cluster_thesis.falsifier: GEV Q3 (2026-10-28) shows gas-turbine slot reservations or electrification orders down QoQ, OR VRT Q3 (2026-10-21) book-to-bill <1.0, OR a top-4 hyperscaler cuts 2027 capex guidance before 2026-11-15.

margin_pool.moving_toward: Scarce, long-lead generating capacity priced at post-2025 rates (GEV 2028+ turbine vintages) and speed-to-power on-site generation that bypasses the interconnection queue (BE); in-hall equipment vendors are buying their way toward power (VRT-UIG).
margin_pool.moving_away_from: In-hall equipment assembly where revenue conversion is supply-chain-bound (VRT Q2 miss), and any fixed-price backlog booked before the 2025 price reset (GEV 2027 vintage).

evidence.claim: GLJ: ~3pp backlog margin on 2027 turbine vintage (ordered 2024, pre-price-hikes) vs 10-11pp on 2025-booked vintage shipping 2028; 2027 Power segment margin 18.5% vs 20.7% consensus
VRT Q2 revenue $3.27B +24% missed by ~$110M, attributed to supply-chain congestion and project execution timing, not orders; EPS beat and guide raised
VRT agreed to buy UtilityInnovation Group (on-site/DC power) for ~$1.45B upfront, up to ~$2.6B with earnouts; UIG revenue/backlog undisclosed
BE: ~$20B total / ~$6B product backlog; FY26 guide raised a third time to $3.9-4.2B revenue; Brookfield financing commitment expanded to $25B

differentiator_reads.read: Behind-the-meter speed-to-power sidesteps interconnection queues; 'all major US hyperscalers' have validated systems per CEO; $20B backlog

Product backlog ~$6B vs FY26 revenue guide $3.9-4.2B = ~1.5yr coverage, so pricing resets pass through fast (GLJ vintage-lag mechanism ~n/a on product); guide raised 3x this year = conversion is happening, not just booking

ranking.case_against: Priced for it: ~95x FY26 non-GAAP EPS mid ($2.70), EV/EBITDA ~199x, +190% YTD, mean target $276.05 only +7.4% above $257.05; beta 1.68 -- highest rate/duration sensitivity in the cluster going into a hike-odds FOMC; ~$14B non-product (service/long-term) backlog is long-dated and could carry exactly the fixed-price vintage lag GLJ describes -- untested, no source.

differentiator_reads.read: Deepest dated backlog (116GW gas, $40.6B electrification, $176B total, >50% of 2031 gas slots booked) but GLJ shows 2027 is the low-margin vintage (~3pp) before 2028's 10-11pp; this is a timing air-pocket, and the 2028 step-up is itself evidence of pricing power
differentiator_reads.source: GEV Q2'26 8-K via prior ladder; GLJ via Investing.com
